hook.text: Wind directly affects takeoff and landing—headwinds help, tailwinds hurt, and crosswinds challenge pilots.

buildup.text: A headwind shortens takeoff distance by increasing airflow over the wings before the plane is even moving fast.

discovery.text: A tailwind does the opposite—the plane needs more ground speed to get the same airflow, lengthening the takeoff roll.

twist.text: Crosswinds require pilots to crab the aircraft—flying sideways into the wind—then straightening just before touchdown.

climax.text: Every aircraft has a maximum demonstrated crosswind component—exceeding it risks losing directional control on landing.

punchline.text: Wind is either your friend or your enemy—direction decides.
